solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hits, back when making Charlie Parker's last dissonant music

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from the end towards the start
one letter is made into another, so a single letter is swapped out here

parts.note: knocks are hits or blows
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the last of something is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A jazz fan complains that Charlie Parker's late recordings turned into discordant noise.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOCKS turned back is SKCONK; its C (Charlie) becomes R (the last letter of Parker), giving SKRONK. Charlie Parker was a jazz saxophonist, which suits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Skronk is a slang term for harsh, abrasive, free-jazz or noise-rock playing, the kind of sound described as discordant.

clue.text: King stuck with rock and roller eternally

definitions.text: King stuck with rock and roller eternally

parts.words: King stuck with rock and roller eternally
parts.note: surface reading: a monarch of pop music forever tied to rock and roll; setter's reading: a king of Greek myth condemned forever to roll a boulder up a hill

explanation.walkthrough: 'King' and 'rock and roller' summon Elvis; read literally, the king is stuck with a rock and is a roller of it for eternity, the punishment of SISYPHUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this king of Corinth was punished in Hades by endlessly pushing a boulder uphill, only for it to roll back down.

clue.text: Old barbarian spearing desert lynx

indicators.note: a spear pierces and sits inside its target, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
O is a standard abbreviation for old
an oik is a boorish, uncouth person

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior impales a wild cat in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy place but is the verb, RAT. An oik is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooikat is the Afrikaans name for the caracal, the red-brown wild cat of Africa also called the desert lynx.

clue.text: Correspondent's stock repetition to copy style in review

indicators.note: to review is to look back over something, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep is one repetition of an exercise
to ape is to copy
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A journalist's stock phrases are repeated in a review, copying another's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondent' suggests a reporter, but here it is a letter-writer, whose stock is paper. REP + APE + TON read backwards gives NOTEPAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter-writer keeps a supply of writing sheets, so their stock in trade is stationery for letters.

clue.text: "X" in audio caught by PAL data verifier

indicators.note: what is caught is held inside the catcher

parts.note: a chum is a pal

indicators.note: audio is what is heard, so the letter is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the letter X said out loud, written phonetically

explanation.surface: A cross mark in the audio track is picked up by a PAL television signal check.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL in capitals suggests the television standard, but it just means friend. The letter X spoken is spelt ECKS, which sits inside CHUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A checksum is a value computed from a block of data so errors in transmission or storage can be detected.

clue.text: Nothing animated bartender in tavern and London station abandoned by sons having similar ends

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the use of similar word endings

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another

parts.note: a hotel serves as an inn or tavern
O looks like zero
Moe runs the bar in the cartoon series The Simpsons

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so letters drop out

parts.note: Euston is a London railway terminus
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A tale of a cartoon barman in a pub and a deserted London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Moe is the barman of Moe's Tavern in The Simpsons, so 'animated' means drawn, not lively. Euston is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhetorical term names the repetition of identical endings in neighbouring words or lines, a figure that can cause copying errors.

clue.text: Copper, French one with line cut in early script

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
F is an abbreviation for French
the Roman numeral for one
the prescription shorthand for 'with' (Latin cum) is a c with a bar over it; cut the bar and a plain C is left

explanation.surface: A French police officer with a line of text cut from an old manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal. The barred c meaning 'with' appears on medical prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cufic, usually spelt Kufic, is the angular early form of Arabic writing used for the first copies of the Koran.

clue.text: N American slacker, to shirk duties of gay people, ignoring conclusions

indicators.note: to ignore the conclusions is to leave off the final letters

parts.note: to skulk is to dodge work
pink is used of things relating to gay people, as in the pink pound

explanation.surface: An American idler dodges the chores of gay housemates, never finishing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces lose their last letter: SKUL(K) + PIN(K).
explanation.definitionFit: Skulpin is a variant of sculpin, a North American spiny fish, also used of a worthless, good-for-nothing person.

clue.text: Successive months devoid of chief soft and large fish in New Zealand

indicators.note: something devoid of a thing is without it, so letters are removed

parts.note: two months that follow one another
Ch is an abbreviation for chief
p is piano, soft in music
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Two months without the boss, spent fishing large in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: MARCH loses CH and APRIL loses P and L, leaving MAR + ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Marari is the Maori name for the butterfish, a food fish of New Zealand waters.

clue.text: Discovered corgi decapitated falcon following rejection of new contraceptive hormone

indicators.note: one part comes after another in the sequence
to reject is to throw back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: novel means new

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is taken off
dis-covered means with its covering removed, so only the inside letters stay

parts.note: corgi without its outer letters
a kestrel is a small falcon

explanation.surface: A dog and a bird of prey are found while a new contraceptive is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like 'found' but means stripped of its outside letters. NOVEL reversed, then ORG, then KESTREL without K.
explanation.definitionFit: Levonorgestrel is a synthetic progestogen used in contraceptive pills, implants and the morning-after pill.

clue.text: Second right taken by flashy car thief to meet male caretaker?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: what is taken is held, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: in Chambers a hotter is a joyrider who steals cars and drives them showily
R is the abbreviation for right
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A flashy car thief takes a second right turn on the way to meet a male caretaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker' looks like a janitor, but a caretaker government or manager holds office only temporarily; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker leader is appointed as a stopgap until a permanent one arrives, so the role is temporary and brief.

clue.text: Diffuse disease resistance doubled

parts.note: flu is a common disease
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, written twice

explanation.surface: A spreading illness becomes twice as hard to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diffuse' reads as an adjective about the disease but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Flurr is an old dialect verb meaning to scatter or spread about, which is what to diffuse means.

clue.text: Lottery down under Pence, otherwise called number two?

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for pence
aka stands for also known as
number two is a childish euphemism for poo

explanation.surface: Is Mike Pence, the American vice-president, known in Australia as the number two in a lottery?
explanation.walkthrough: Pence looks like the vice-president, a literal 'number two', but it is just pennies, and 'number two' is the nursery word for faeces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakapoo is an Australian name for a Chinese-style lottery played with slips marked with characters.

clue.text: Term for one with hasty departure, having run away?

definitions.text: Term for one with hasty departure
definitions.meaning: surface reading: a word for someone who leaves in a rush
setter's reading: a word for a hasty departure with R for run tacked on, describing a fugitive

explanation.walkthrough: A word for a hasty departure plus R (run) gives ESCAPER, and the whole clue also describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has fled captivity or broken free from confinement is a fugitive, and this is the plain agent noun.

clue.text: What precedes locum's final training with surgery in mind?

parts.note: the final letter of locum is M, and the letter that precedes it in that word is U
PT is physical training
OP is short for operation, a piece of surgery

explanation.surface: A question about what a stand-in doctor's last stretch of training should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as medical training, but 'What precedes locum's final' is a letter puzzle: the letter just before the M at the end of LOCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Up top is an informal idiom for the head or brain, so something up top is held in the mind.

clue.text: Excessive wine overruns a small flute

parts.note: OTT is over the top
taken as written
vino is informal for wine

explanation.surface: Too much wine spills over and swamps a little flute glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overruns' places the wine after A. A flute is also a tall wine glass, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottavino is the Italian name for the piccolo, the high-pitched little flute sounding an octave above the ordinary one.

clue.text: Mormons fell in even after adapting a bit of footwear from Durban

definitions.text: a bit of footwear from Durban

indicators.note: one thing is placed inside another
adapting changes a thing's form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
LDS stands for the Latter-day Saints, the Mormon church
to KO is to knock out or fell

explanation.surface: Mormons fell into line once they adapted a South African shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall but is the verb meaning knock down. Durban is a city in South Africa, signalling an Afrikaans word.
explanation.definitionFit: Veldskoen is the South African name for a rough rawhide ankle boot, so one is a single item of footwear.

clue.text: Payout for basset from exotic pet tax being reduced in South Australia

indicators.note: one thing is placed inside another

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the state of South Australia

indicators.note: something exotic is foreign and strange, so the letters take an unfamiliar order
reduced means made shorter, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: A basset hound's owner gets a payout from a reduced tax on exotic pets in South Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Basset looks like the dog but is an old card game, which is why the answer is so obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old card game of basset a septleva was a winning bet paying seven times the stake.

clue.text: Return of tartare sauce with meat left Australian wild

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: steak tartare is served raw
ragu is an Italian meat sauce
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A diner sends back tartare sauce and leftover meat to an Australian bush kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tartare sauce' reads as one condiment, but tartare gives RAW and the sauce is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Warragul, or warrigal, is an Aboriginal-derived Australian word for the dingo, and as an adjective means untamed.

clue.text: Waves over companion missing island's large dragonflies

definitions.note: the answer is a genus name, standing for the group as a whole

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning over flips the letters to run upwards

parts.note: the sea is a mass of waves

indicators.note: what is missing has been taken out

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Waves wash over a friend left behind by an island's big dragonflies.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA turned over, then CHINA without its I. In Cockney rhyming slang, china (plate) means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschna is the scientific genus of the big hawker dragonflies, which are among the largest flying insects in Britain.

clue.text: Part of Philippines portrayed by Shirley Temple

indicators.note: what is portrayed is shown within the picture, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: runs across the two words of the name

explanation.surface: Did the child film star Shirley Temple once play a role set in the Philippines?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of Shirley and the start of Temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Leyte is an island in the eastern Visayas of the Philippines, scene of a great naval battle in 1944.

clue.text: Yachtsman primarily catching fish clear of a keelboat

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of yachtsman

indicators.note: being clear of something means being rid of it, so a letter goes

parts.note: angling is catching fish with a rod
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor sets out fishing from a keelboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' looks like a container signal, but 'catching fish' is the pastime, which then loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yngling is a small Norwegian-designed three-person racing keelboat, once sailed in the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Lady's fingers lifting ball and cat

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: an orb is a ball or sphere
mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A woman's fingers pick up a ball and a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady's fingers' seems to be a hand; it is the vegetable. ORB + MOG read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's fingers is a British name for okra, whose pods are also called gumbo or gombro.

clue.text: Bossing about old seals

indicators.note: about means round and round, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordering about elderly seals as if they were circus animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' looks like the animals but is the verb, and 'old' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsign is an obsolete verb meaning to confirm with a stamp or sign, so it once meant authenticating a document.

clue.text: Religious warrior's bullying in a cycle, obliterating an unspecified number

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves a letter from one end of the word to the other
to obliterate is to wipe out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: hazing is the bullying of newcomers
n stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A religious fighter's harassment goes round and round, wiping out countless victims.
explanation.walkthrough: HAZING loses N to give HAZIG, then its final G moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghazi is an Arabic title for a Muslim fighter against unbelievers, a champion of the faith in holy war.

clue.text: Reform hustings mostly not observed previously

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reassembled
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Election reform at the hustings has mostly gone unnoticed before.
explanation.walkthrough: Hustings are election meetings in Britain. Drop the final S, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsight is an old adjective meaning unseen or unexamined, so it once described something not looked at.

clue.text: Black tea — that's disappointing for core of tasters?

definitions.text: Black tea — that's disappointing for core of tasters?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece replaces another in the word tea

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so the middle letter of tasters is wanted

parts.note: its middle letter, the fourth of seven, is T
OH is the exclamation of someone let down

explanation.surface: A tea-tasting panel finds a black tea a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: In TEA the T, the core of 'tasters', is replaced by OH, giving OHEA after B for black. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a black tea whose tasting disappoints.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, once the name for the finest and later for the cheapest grade.

clue.text: Surveyor's tool needs right hand to displace the stone

indicators.note: to displace is to push something out and take its place

parts.note: a theodolite measures angles in surveying
RH is the abbreviation for right hand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surveyor's instrument needs a right-hand man to shift a boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The stone' looks like the definition, but THE is part of the wordplay, replaced by RH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodolite is a pale rose-red or purple variety of garnet prized as a gem.

clue.text: Colourful songbird swallowing very advanced insect's egg-tube

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: the oriole is a brightly coloured songbird
V is the abbreviation for very
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: A bright songbird gulps down an insect's egg.
explanation.walkthrough: V + A go inside ORIOLE after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovariole is one of the tubules that make up an insect's ovary, in which the eggs develop.

clue.text: Older evening primroses covering famous mausoleum site

parts.note: on top of, so covering
Agra in India is home to the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Old evening primroses grow over the grounds of a famous tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Older' signals a former botanical name.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagra is the old genus name for the evening primrose family, now classed as Oenothera.
